name: Charlotte Adigéry & Bolis Pupul
label: DEEWEE
lede: Two Ghent friends of a decade were paired by a pair of DJs for a film soundtrack, and ended up with an album about microaggressions you can dance to.

eras.title: Two Ghent kids, separate tracks
eras.text: Before they were a duo, Bolis Pupul was in a synthpop band with his sister, and Charlotte Adigéry was studying music in Hasselt. They knew each other from Ghent, nothing more.

years.h: Boris Zeebroek's band Hong Kong Dong enters Humo's Rock Rally
years.p: The synthpop group, which Zeebroek ran with his sister and brother-in-law, entered Belgium's best-known young-band contest. He would later record as [[Bolis Pupul|52f78c75-9f2f-4353-a368-ac35e96ca25a]].
years.xp:
Zeebroek is the son of the Belgian cartoonist Kamagurka and Yu Wei Wun, who was born in Hong Kong and moved to Belgium at seven. According to Wikipedia, she died in a car accident in June 2008, and the band's momentum faded afterward.

The stage name is family shorthand: Wikipedia says "Bolis" is how his maternal grandmother said Boris, and "Pupul" was a sound his father made to get him to sleep.

years.h: Hong Kong Dong finally release their first album
years.p: Four years after the Rock Rally, the band put out its debut. Pupul's real career would start somewhere else: Soulwax's studio.

eras.title: The Dewaeles make the introduction
eras.text: A film soundtrack put both of them in the same studio as the Dewaele brothers of Soulwax, and DEEWEE became the home for everything that followed. The duo's first records were credited to Charlotte alone.

q: When Stephen and David said that we should work together, we didn't even question it.
years.src: NME interview · The Line of Best Fit
years.h: Belgica: a soundtrack and a blind date
years.p: Soulwax's [[David Dewaele|b4209bc6-ad50-4f97-aec1-d162f222018f]] and [[Stephen Dewaele|39b125d7-b8dd-47bc-8339-0e5e2b711390]] score Felix Van Groeningen's film Belgica. Charlotte Adigéry sings on "The Best Thing"; Pupul is already on their label.
years.xp:
The pair knew each other only casually from Ghent. The Line of Best Fit reports Adigéry was stuck with writer's block at DEEWEE, surrounded by, in her words, geniuses, when the Dewaeles told her to get in a room with Pupul.

NME quotes her on the suggestion: she and Pupul did not even question it. Pupul calls them "professional friendship soulmates."

years.h: A self-titled Charlotte Adigéry EP lands on DEEWEE
years.p: Sung in English, French and Creole, and made with Pupul, but credited to Adigéry alone. That credit stuck in her throat later.
years.xp: DIY reports that when they made Topical Dancer they insisted on equal billing because they felt misunderstood when earlier work presented Pupul as just her producer.

years.h: Zandoli EP: mixed by the Dewaeles, sold to HBO
years.p: The Dewaeles co-produced and mixed it. "Paténipat" ended up in the trailer for HBO's The New Pope.

years.h: "High Lights" gets UK radio and a passport stamp
years.p: NME says the single earned UK radio play and led to shows in London and New York. Adigéry also toured with Neneh Cherry and made NME's 2019 Essential New Artists.

eras.title: Topical Dancer
eras.text: After Zandoli, Soulwax told them to make a full album. They did, with Charlotte visibly pregnant for the whole process, and it made year-end lists on both sides of the Atlantic.

years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.2 and ranked it No. 22 on its list of 2022's best albums. It was released on DEEWEE on March 4, 2022, and peaked at No. 2 on the Ultratop Flanders chart.
years.xp:
Co-written and co-produced by Soulwax, it runs 13 tracks across English, French, Dutch and Creole. Wikipedia lists Metacritic at 85 from six reviews, and The Observer called it a banging fusion of funk, house and techno.

Paste later placed it at No. 232 on its list of the 250 greatest albums of the 21st century so far (October 2025).

years.big: We don't want to stay bitter
q: We don't want to stay bitter.
years.src: DIY · The Line of Best Fit
years.p: The album takes on colonial leftovers, misogyny and social media pile-ons with house grooves.
years.xp:
DIY says "Blenda" is about being asked where you are really from, a question Adigéry has heard all her life in Belgium. "Esperanto" takes both sides of the language-policing argument, and the closer "Thank You" answers every condescending remark from her career in one go.

The Line of Best Fit reports they thought of the record as a time capsule of 2021 meant to be opened in 50 years.

years.src: Wikipedia: Topical Dancer · The Line of Best Fit
years.h: Adigéry's mother, Christiane, sings on "Ich Mwen"
years.p: A duet on womanhood and motherhood, on a record Adigéry made while pregnant. Her newborn came along on the press run, The Line of Best Fit reports.

years.h: "Thank You" becomes the club hit about unwanted opinions
years.p: FLOOD called the single a club hit about unwanted opinions. The official video is on YouTube.

eras.title: Festivals, then a solo letter
eras.text: The live show catches up with the record, and Pupul steps out on his own for a DEEWEE album about his mother.

years.h: Libera Awards nominate Topical Dancer for Best Electronic Record
years.p: The American independent-music awards put the album on the 2023 shortlist.

years.h: Glastonbury: a Sunday on Worthy Farm
years.p: The duo play Glastonbury on June 25, 2023, per setlist.fm, and a performance of "Mantra" from the set is on video.

years.h: Best Kept Secret: the festival set on video
years.p: A full set filmed at the festival in 2023 shows the live show.

years.h: Bolis Pupul's Letter to Yu, a solo album for his mother
years.p: Pupul wrote it after visiting Hong Kong in 2018 and writing to his mother, Yu Wei Wun, on the street where she was born. Pitchfork gave it 8, and Stephen and David Dewaele encouraged the project.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, he shared the letter and demos with the Dewaeles, who pushed him to make a full album at their Ghent studio. Resident Advisor's Marshall Gu described Detroit techno and Kraftwerk-style synth pop with Hong Kong field recordings.

It peaked at No. 9 on the Ultratop Flanders chart.
